diagram_math_checks.evidence: Each drawn P and Q has exactly three boxes, filled once by 1,2,3; rows run top to bottom and boxes are left aligned. All twelve tableaux have strictly increasing rows and columns, agreeing with the local tableau convention. No morphisms or commutative relations are asserted.

123 successively appends in row 1 at (1,1),(1,2),(1,3), so P=Q=[123]. In 321 each next letter bumps the complete existing column down: shapes grow at (1,1),(2,1),(3,1), giving P=Q=[1/2/3]. This is the row-insertion definition and verification step 1.1.

132: 1 then 3 gives [13]; inserting 2 bumps 3 to row 2, so P=[12/3], creation positions (1,1),(1,2),(2,1), Q=[12/3]. 213: 1 bumps 2 after initial [2], then 3 appends in row 1, so P=[13/2], creation positions (1,1),(2,1),(1,2), Q=[13/2].

231: [2] then [23], then 1 replaces/bump 2, so P=[13/2]; creation positions (1,1),(1,2),(2,1), Q=[12/3]. 312: [3], then [1/3], then 2 appends to row 1, so P=[12/3]; creation positions (1,1),(2,1),(1,2), Q=[13/2]. Recording labels are times, not letter values, as specified in the recording-tableau lemma used by the correspondence.

The drawn row lengths are (3),(2,1),(2,1),(2,1),(2,1),(1,1,1), hence counts 1,4,1 and uniform probabilities 1/6,4/6,1/6 exactly as verification steps 2.1 and 3.1. The complete original finite computation remains before Remarks and does not invoke the figure.
